Complete every yellow answer cell. You may work one sheet at a time and pause between sheets. Record your actual time in the Timing sheet.

Judge only what is shown in each row. You do not need to know the complete model or suggest a replacement unless the sheet asks what should happen instead. Notes are optional but useful when you choose Partial, No, With concern, or Incorrect.

Choose Partial when the proposal is partly right but too broad, too narrow, incomplete, or imprecise. Choose With concern when a treatment may be acceptable for the main model but loses or weakens useful information.
Choose Unsure when the term is ambiguous, the information conflicts, or the question falls outside your expertise. Unsure is a valid answer and is better than guessing.

Judge the complete plain-language definition as Correct, Partly correct, Incorrect, or Unsure.

For Partly correct or Incorrect, choose the main problem: Wrong general type; Missing or wrong defining feature; Too broad; Too narrow; Unclear wording; Other; or Unsure. Leave this field blank for Correct.
Judge each geological statement as Generally true, Context-specific, Partly wrong, Incorrect, or Unsure.
Generally true means the relationship normally holds. Context-specific means it holds only in some geological settings. A statement beginning 'For this named item' concerns only that particular item.
Judge the statement itself using your geological knowledge. No source excerpt is shown because a local occurrence could be mistaken for a general rule.
Judge whether the term names one specific basin, field, formation, time interval, structure, or other particular item rather than a reusable kind.
A formally named and bounded geological age or stage is treated as one specific time interval. A general descriptive interval is a reusable kind unless it refers to one explicitly bounded interval.
Judge whether the proposed geological type is correct. You are not shown the complete type vocabulary and do not need to select a replacement; explain in Notes only when useful.

The main model contains reusable concepts needed to compare Brazilian Pre-Salt systems, especially geological objects, materials, structures, processes, spatial arrangement, boundaries, stratigraphic units, petrophysical properties, and geological time. Narrow local variants, individual measurements, and paper-specific details may stay in extensions instead.

Compare the term's original meaning with how it is represented now. Choose Fully when the important geological meaning remains, Mostly when some important detail is weakened or lost, No when the meaning is not retained, or Unsure.

Separately decide whether the new treatment is suitable for the main Pre-Salt model: Yes, With concern, No, or Unsure. A treatment may suit the main model even when a narrow detail moves to an extension.
Leaving a term out does not mean it is geologically false. It means the information is too narrow for the main model or is represented somewhere else.
A term may be kept as a property or relationship instead of a separate concept. Judge whether the new wording still makes the important geological information available.
Choose an answer only when geological meaning is Mostly preserved or not preserved: keep the term separately; keep its information without a separate term; leave it out; or Unsure.
Use Notes for concise geological reasoning when the bounded choices do not capture an important issue. Thank you for your expertise.
